source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Begin at the most contaminated area and move toward cleaner tissue using fresh supplies for each pass.","B":"Move repeatedly between dirty and clean areas as long as a new swab is used each time.","C":"Clean areas in random order because sterile gloves eliminate the need for a clean-to-dirty sequence.","D":"Begin at the least contaminated area and move toward more contaminated tissue without returning used material to cleaner areas."}}
source_row.rationale: Aseptic wound-care sequencing follows a clean-to-dirty principle: begin with the least contaminated area and move toward more contaminated areas without carrying organisms back to cleaner tissue. Option D is correct. A and B reverse that principle, and C ignores contamination control.
source_row.source_detail: Aseptic sequencing/wound care: proceed from clean to dirty, moving from least contaminated toward more contaminated areas and avoiding transfer of organisms back toward cleaner tissue; use clean/sterile supplies appropriately. Current NCBI Bookshelf Nursing Skills wound-care content live-rechecked 2026-08-15; CDC sources were checked and do not provide a more specific clean-to-dirty wound-sequencing statement. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
